probe.summary: A probe run asks Plex cheap aggregate questions (COUNT and MAX/SUM per extracted table), and fingerprints the answers together with the report's YAML and view SQL. If the fingerprint equals the last clean run's, extraction and view creation are skipped; otherwise the full pipeline runs. It exists because every pipeline is a full WRITE_TRUNCATE refresh (99 full table pulls), so four prod runs a day need a cheap change check. Label Design pioneered it on 2026-10-01. Measured on Plex test: 82 probe queries took 12.4 s in total.
steps: The dispatcher or a scheduler starts the Cloud Run job; RUN_MODE is probe, full, scheduled or retry.
main() loads the YAML from GCS and opens the Plex ODBC connection.
probe_kind returns auto (probe_mode: auto), explicit (a probe.queries block, Label Design) or none.
may_skip is true for RUN_MODE=probe, and for an explicit probe on a scheduled run; false for full, retry, and scheduled auto-probe runs.
ensure_probe_log_table, then last_applied_probe reads the newest applied fingerprint and snapshot.
run_probe runs one aggregate per extraction and hashes the sorted snapshot plus the config and SQL hash (sha256, 32 chars).
If may_skip and the fingerprint is unchanged: log skipped, record dispatch outcome skipped, send the short 'Probe ran - nothing to update' email unless EMAIL_MODE=on_error.
Otherwise run every extraction and create or replace the views (a failed view is retried once).
After a clean run write probe_log applied; a partial or failed run writes failed and the reference does not advance.
record_dispatch_outcome writes the outcome onto the etl_dispatch_log row; the full email names the changed tables.
probe.change_detection: COUNT(*) catches added or removed rows. The extraction's probe: [...] list adds MAX(change date or key) columns (88 of the 100 auto extractions across 13 pipelines have one, after the 2026-10-21 audit) and sum:Col entries for SUM, which makes edits visible on views with no change date; SUM of key columns is refused (Plex 32-bit overflow) and Plex refuses SUM on bit columns. Columns were chosen by scripts/generate_probe_columns.py. YAML (_config_sha) and every view's SQL are in the fingerprint. Floats are rounded to 4 places. The YAML key is probe_mode, not probe:, because older images crash on a string probe:. Label Design uses an explicit probe.queries block instead: 4 queries (Label Design release status keys, their releases, the Pending Fulfillment status key, and the orders the view would push), so an order approval alone moves the fingerprint (L14, 2026-10-20).
probe.failure_policy: No retries: prod max_retries is 0 and the prod -retry schedulers are gone. A failed, partial or lost run gets ONE follow-up probe from the dispatcher 15 minutes later (not if older than 6 hours; never a follow-up of a follow-up; a busy follow-up is not retried; a dispatch-failed start gets none). A failed run does not advance the fingerprint, so the follow-up re-runs in full. The probe fails open: a query error, bad column, empty aggregate or unreadable probe_log runs the full extraction and logs an inconclusive row.
gotchas: A quiet probe skips view creation, so a SQL-only deploy used to wait for Plex to change (OPEN_ITEMS L10). Since 2026-10-19 YAML and SQL are in the fingerprint; L10 stays open until the next SQL-only deploy proves it (the quiet run must log applied).
Code and image changes are not in the fingerprint; a quiet pipeline picks them up at the next changed probe, the 4 AM full run, or a hand start.

An edit on a table with no change date and no sum: column is invisible to the probe; the 4 AM full run bounds it at one day. Known cases after the 2026-10-21 audit: a requisition status flip (Requisition_Status_Key is refused as key-like; needs a main.py allowlist) and a rep reassignment in Sales_v_Order_Salesperson.
A permanently broken probe is invisible: query probe_log WHERE outcome='inconclusive'.
Busy tables (Part_v_Production, Part_v_Container) mean Work Orders and inventory usually run in full at 1 PM and 6 PM; that is correct.
A short email does not mean views were rebuilt, and job exit 0 does not mean the view exists; query it.
The first run after a fingerprint format change always runs in full.

A failed run used to be followed by a skip if Plex stayed quiet (Label Design, 2026-10-20 22:02 UTC). last_run_unclean (image 9d1d62b) makes the next probe run in full; not yet seen working in prod (D14 d).
probe.prod_vs_test: Only prod uses the probe to skip work. The dispatcher starts prod jobs with RUN_MODE=probe at 1 PM, 6 PM and 11 PM, and an unchanged fingerprint skips the run; the 4 AM run is RUN_MODE=full and never skips. Test jobs are started by Cloud Scheduler with no override, so RUN_MODE is scheduled: the probe still runs and its fingerprint is logged as the reference, but probe_may_skip returns false and the job extracts everything, every night. That keeps test a full nightly rehearsal of every query. The one exception is Label Design, whose explicit probe skips on scheduled runs in both environments.

steps: Work on your project's dev branch in its own worktree (ptbq-dev = dev, ptbq-scorecard = dev-scorecard, ptbq-sandbox = dev-sandbox, ptbq-label-design = dev-label-design); the primary folder C:\F\Parasol\plex-to-big-query is main, for merge and deploy only.
Commit with a CHANGELOG.md entry plus the matching docs/reports or reports-list update; change prod and test YAML together; stage by explicit path.
Open a PR into main and merge it (pushing a dev branch into main is blocked); make sure main is pushed so HEAD equals origin/main.

Config, SQL and infra: run ./scripts/deploy.sh from the primary folder. It runs deploy_preflight.sh, checks HEAD == origin/main, terraform plan -var-file=terraform.tfvars -out (tf_guard.py runs inside), prints plan_review.py (content changes vs line-ending noise, destroys flagged), asks you to type the change count, applies exactly that plan, then tags deploy/<UTC timestamp> and pushes it.

Python code ships as an image through Cloud Build: gcloud builds submit --config deploy/cloudbuild.yaml --project=voxdatalake --substitutions=SHORT_SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) . Steps: fetch-driver, build, push-sha, push-latest, deploy-all (every job in _ALL_JOBS, 30 jobs), smoke-test on the TEST job only. Terraform jobs ignore image changes.
Cloud Functions use gcloud functions deploy (commands in main.tf comments); Apps Script apps are pasted by hand. Prod schedule changes are SQL on PlexOps.etl_schedule.
Verify: terraform plan on clean main should list nothing; query the BigQuery view after a run; read PlexOps.etl_dispatch_log for prod.
guards: pre-commit: the folder must be on its own branch (override ALLOW_WRONG_FOLDER=1).
pre-commit: no non-merge commits on main (ALLOW_MAIN_COMMIT=1).
pre-commit: a dev branch carries only its own project's files and one commit may not mix projects (ALLOW_CROSS_PROJECT=1).
pre-commit: changes under reports/ or terraform/ (non-.md) need a staged CHANGELOG.md (ALLOW_NO_CHANGELOG=1).
pre-commit: prod and test YAML plex_view counts must match (ALLOW_YAML_MISMATCH=1).
pre-push: only local main goes to origin main, and no non-fast-forward push to main (ALLOW_MAIN_PUSH=1).
tf_guard.py runs on every terraform plan and apply and refuses unless: primary worktree, branch main, clean tree, HEAD == origin/main. TF_GUARD_OVERRIDE="reason" is for read-only plans only.
deploy.sh adds preflight, HEAD == origin/main, plan_review.py and a typed change count.
Never --no-verify; use an override only when the user explicitly wants the exception, and say so.

label_design.overview: Label Design keeps the design team's Monday queue filled from Plex. When a sales order line that needs label artwork reaches Pending Fulfillment, it appears on the Monday board Plex Import Test, about an hour after approval, with the customer, part, order, priority, reps, bottle and label details filled in. The team moves each item to Design & QA and works it there.
push_steps: Gate: count view rows whose LCR the push log has never recorded. 0 = stop, no Monday call.
Read Plex Import Test's columns by title and type (22 mapped).
Dedupe: skip a line whose LCR (first 12 hex of SHA-256 of order|line) is on the board or in the push log for ANY board.
Alarm: more than 60 new lines at once = keys broke; nothing pushed, email.

Align label colours with Design & QA for every status label this run writes (labels.py). A risk of a WRONG label stops the run before anything is created; a refused label on Design & QA only means the field will arrive blank.
Create items with create_labels_if_missing off; one bad value retries column by column so only that value is lost.
Write every attempt to label_design_push_log (created, partial, failed).
Email problems and labels added to Design & QA, once a day per problem (outcome = alert rows).

colour_rule.summary: A Monday board move carries a status value across by the label's COLOUR, not its name or id. The destination shows its label with that colour; if it has none, the column's default (blank for Bottle Material, Normal for Priority).
colour_rule.evidence: Proven 2026-10-27: 10 test items covering every pushed label were moved from Plex Import Test to a structure-only copy of Design & QA. Before recolouring, 12 of 48 status values arrived lost or as another label (PET and HDPE blank, 4 Reason Codes and 3 Inside Sales Reps swapped, Julianni Pacheco as N/A). After giving Plex Import Test Design & QA's colours, 1 of 48: RUSH ⚠️️, a label Plex never sends.
colour_rule.damage: Before the fix, every item moved from the old board showed Priority Normal instead of Medium, and 8 showed another Reason Code; Bottle Material arrived blank and was refilled by the repair job. 45 values were listed for the team on 2026-10-27 (OPEN_ITEMS L16).
colour_rule.keep_it: The push aligns colours itself before each run that creates items. A label added by hand to one board needs the same colour on the other.

label_design.email_note: Subject [Plex ETL] - Sales: Label Design push, to the ETL's recipients. At most once a day per problem. A clean push sends nothing; the ETL's own email covers a run that could not start the push.

runbook.q: What did the push do today?
runbook.a: Read the push log (alert rows are emails sent).
runbook.sql:
SELECT pushed_at, outcome, order_number, customer_part_no, monday_item_id, detail
FROM `voxdatalake.PlexProd.label_design_push_log`
WHERE DATE(pushed_at, 'America/Denver') = CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver')
ORDER BY pushed_at DESC;

runbook.q: An item on Design & QA shows a blank or different status
runbook.a: Compare it with what was sent (column_values in the push log), then look the label up in the colour catalog below. A colour that differs between the boards is the cause; the next push that writes to that column fixes the colour, or fix it by hand on Plex Import Test.
runbook.sql:
SELECT pushed_at, column_values FROM `voxdatalake.PlexProd.label_design_push_log`
WHERE monday_item_id = '<item id>' AND outcome IN ('created', 'partial');

runbook.q: Someone added a label by hand
runbook.a: Give it the same colour on both boards, or leave it: the push adds a label Plex sends to both boards itself.
python scripts/hub/label_colours.py (add --check to fail on drift), then python scripts/hub/build_hub.py.

runbook.q: Test the push without writing anything
runbook.a: BQ_DATASET=PlexProd MONDAY_BOARD_ID=18437236736 DRY_RUN=1 python -m label_design_service.push (needs MONDAY_API_KEY). Shows what it would create and any label colour change.

runbook.q: A new order is not on the board
runbook.a: Check, in order: the order is Pending Fulfillment with a Label Design release and dated on or after 2026-10-18 (label_design_report); the ODBC copy lags Plex by about 50 min; the probe ran (probe_log); the push log for the order; a Label Design push email.

traps: Design & QA has two status columns titled Sales Rep. The first (color_mm076254) holds the rep and is the one the push and a move use; color_mm7zxq8m is always empty.
Priority on Design & QA is restricted: the API key cannot add labels there. A new Priority from Plex would arrive blank on a move and the push emails it.
Monday's items(ids) still returns deleted and archived items; check state.
LCR is the dedupe mark written into each item. Clearing it by hand does not cause a re-push: the push log also counts.
Plex dates are naive Mountain time; the prod ODBC copy runs about 50 minutes behind Plex.
